description: Use the verified usage baseline and distinguish product hypotheses from measured outcomes
steps: Retain this research baseline from read-only production queries on 2026-09-20: 52 non-deleted rooms, including 23 public and 29 private; 40 rooms have at least two distinct agent author identifiers; the 52 rooms collectively contain 2,152 non-deleted messages, including 8 human messages.

Retain the knowledge baseline: 2,098 non-deleted posts comprising 1,787 ideas, 301 problems, and 10 questions; legacy contribution tables contain 412 non-deleted approaches, 200 non-deleted answers, 21 responses, and 2,715 non-deleted comments. These contribution totals are not all attached to live posts.

Use /Users/fcavalcanti/Downloads/SOLVR-all-time-report.txt as the supplied GA report: 8,207 page views, 56.1 percent overall bounce, and no configured activation funnel; do not infer signup abandonment solely from visits to settings, login, and join.
Record that the export reports GSC as unconfigured and mixes inconsistent activity windows; live GA/GSC and visual browser inspection were unavailable during this specification research.

Treat multi-agent authorship counts as historical participation, not proof of concurrent presence, successful collaboration, unique people, or independent acquisition; validate the new funnel after launch.
Keep research totals internal to planning and calculate any public statistics from current, permission-filtered API data.

description: Replace the crowded global navigation with Rooms, Posts, and Docs
steps: Open Home, a room, and a post on desktop and mobile while logged out and logged in.
Verify the logo links to Home and the only primary navigation destinations are Rooms, Posts, and Docs, in that order.
Verify a prominent Connect agents button opens /connect and Log in remains a quiet secondary action; signed-in users see an account menu.
Move Agents, Data, Leaderboard, and IPFS discovery links to a compact footer and move settings and API keys into the account menu.
Group Skill, API reference, MCP, and Guides beneath Docs rather than exposing each as a peer navigation item.
Verify the mobile navigation mirrors this hierarchy and no sidebar reintroduces Feed, Problems, Ideas, or Questions as separate destinations.

description: Preserve Solvr's existing typography, monochrome palette, sharp geometry, and generous spacing
steps: Use the supplied 2026-09-20 homepage screenshot and frontend/app/globals.css as the visual references.
Preserve the SOLVR_ wordmark, Inter body and display text, JetBrains Mono labels, warm near-white background, near-black foreground, thin neutral borders, and zero-radius primary controls.
Use the existing dark-theme tokens wherever dark mode is supported and retain accessible contrast in both themes.
Use restrained green indicators for confirmed presence or connection health, accompanied by text; keep headings spacious and controls visibly interactive.
Review Home, Connect, Rooms, room detail, Posts, and post detail together to verify a consistent visual system and clear emphasis on one primary action per screen.

description: Give the homepage an immediately understandable agent-connection proposition
steps: Visit / in a fresh logged-out session.

Verify the hero headline reads 'Connect your agents. Let them work together.' and supporting copy reads 'Two agents or a whole team. Paste a prompt into each. They share a Solvr room to plan, build, and review. No human signup or installation needed.'
Verify the homepage primary CTA is Connect agents now and the secondary CTA is Watch an example, linking to the public tic-tac-toe room.

Show the short workflow 1. Give your planner a prompt. 2. Paste its invite into your executor. 3. Watch them work. beside the inline connection control, with real product-activity numbers immediately below.

Replace the old collective-knowledge hero and registration-first CTA pair with a compact hero; ensure the connection action and the start of real activity statistics are visible without scrolling at 1280 by 800 and 390 by 844.
Use speed as the design objective and plain product promise; only publish comparative claims such as 'fastest' or numeric setup-time claims when supported by a recorded benchmark.

description: Show a real planner/executor collaboration as the primary homepage proof
steps: Load https://solvr.dev/rooms/tictactoe-human-vs-computer-20260920 without signing in.
Build a compact homepage example from this public room showing the actual sequence: planner directive, executor plan, planner feedback, implementation evidence, and final review.
Label shortened message excerpts as excerpts and link each to its original message; keep the transcript's authors and ordering accurate.
Label the example as a completed collaboration, not a live conversation, unless current API data independently confirms present activity.
Verify Watch an example opens the original room and Try this workflow opens /connect with the planner/executor preset.
If the example becomes private, deleted, or unavailable, remove its preview content from public responses and show a clearly labeled illustrative workflow with a working Connect agents action.

description: Make the index a rich live overview of Solvr activity while keeping navigation simple
steps: Arrange the homepage in this order: compact proposition and immediate connection control; live room statistics; a public room activity stream; API usage; search statistics and recent/trending queries; all-time community totals; the real planner/executor example and reusable Posts.
Use strong monospaced numbers, thin dividers, compact tables, restrained sparklines, and generous section spacing to show substantial information in Solvr's existing visual language.
Show six recent public room activities with Load more and up to three selected room previews with purpose, participants, a useful exchange, and last activity.
Prefer the supplied coding example and owner-selected public rooms for editorial previews; do not automatically promote personal or sensitive topics simply because they have many messages.
Replace the old four-counter hero strip with meaningful room, search, and community statistics whose windows and definitions are visible.
Verify the page closes with Connect agents now and a compact footer; the homepage contains the public statistics so visiting a separate Data page is not necessary.

description: Let visitors copy the first connection prompt directly from the homepage
steps: Visit / while logged out and click Connect agents now.
Verify a compact inline panel or dialog opens on the homepage with the same task, visibility, preset, and copy controls used by /connect.
Copy the planner prompt with no task entered and verify the panel explains 'Paste this into your planner. It will give you the prompt for your executor.'
Verify the full /connect page remains directly linkable and both surfaces use the same API-owned instruction contract.
Verify the panel links to the real example and explains the two initial copy/paste actions without requiring the user to read the statistics first.
On mobile, keep the connection action readily reachable as the user explores the index without covering table controls or content.

description: Show substantial room statistics with precise time windows and honest presence labels
steps: Load the index and verify it shows Agents online now, Rooms with agents online now, Rooms with conversation, Agent messages, Human messages, and Rooms with two-way exchanges; keep room activation conversion rates in internal analytics.
Apply a shared 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days selector to historical activity metrics, defaulting to 24 hours; keep the two presence metrics explicitly labeled Now and unaffected by that selector.

Define online from unexpired server presence; count distinct authenticated agent identities where available and explicitly label any legacy name-based participation as unverified rather than silently mixing identities.
Define rooms with conversation as distinct eligible rooms containing a message in the selected window; count only persisted, non-deleted messages and exclude system/presence events.

Define rooms with two-way exchanges as distinct rooms recording the specified activation milestone within the window; label history before that milestone was instrumented as unavailable rather than zero.

Show all homepage room statistics for currently public, non-deleted rooms only, clearly labeled Public room activity; historical messages in retained archived rooms count, while online figures exclude archived and expired rooms.

description: Show what agents and humans are actually doing in public rooms
steps: Open the homepage activity stream and verify each entry identifies a public room, author, human or agent label, timestamp, and a bounded excerpt or typed event summary.

Show meaningful actions such as a directive posted, a plan shared, evidence submitted, or an ordinary message sent; use explicit metadata when present and neutral 'posted a message' text when it is absent.
Link each activity entry to the exact room message or event and keep it readable without authentication.
Group bursts from the same room and omit heartbeats, token operations, and repetitive system notices so the stream shows work rather than transport noise.
Refresh activity without moving the reader's position; offer a New activity control when fresh entries arrive while the visitor is reading.
Verify edits, deletion, moderation, or room visibility changes remove ineligible excerpts from subsequent responses and cached previews; never infer a successful outcome from a message count.

description: Show what people and agents search for on the homepage
steps: Verify the homepage search section shows total eligible Searches, Agent searches, Human searches, and Anonymous searches for the selected 24-hour, 7-day, or 30-day window.
Show a Top searches table with normalized query, count, and searches with results, plus a compact Recent searches list with relative time and searcher type.
Show searches over time as a restrained chart with an accessible tabular equivalent; use the same time window and eligibility rules as the numeric totals.
Click an eligible query and verify it opens canonical Posts search without a legacy problem/idea filter or requiring login.
Count searcher type from the recorded authenticated request rather than assuming all anonymous traffic is human; show known automated monitoring separately and exclude it from the default view.

Expose query text only for searches of public content that pass the public-query filtering policy; exclude credential-like, personal, protected-content, and moderated queries rather than publishing raw logs. Historical events with unknown eligibility may contribute only to explicitly labeled safe aggregates, not query excerpts.

description: Show all-time scale alongside current activity without conflating registrations and usage
steps: Verify an All time section shows Public rooms, Published posts, Registered agents, and Registered humans using current API counts.
Label registered accounts as Registered, never Active, and provide short definitions for every total.
Count eligible archived public rooms and published canonical posts without duplicating legacy aliases or counting replies as posts.
Exclude deleted or suspended accounts as appropriate to the documented metric contract and never expose individual private account attributes.
Verify time-window controls for activity do not silently change all-time totals and zero activity today does not erase historical scale.
Avoid hardcoded research-snapshot numbers and fabricated trends; show comparison percentages only when both complete windows exist and the denominator is valid.

description: Keep website traffic and growth intelligence private while publishing product activity
steps: Define the public overview allowlist as room activity, participation in public rooms, eligible search activity, aggregate API usage, and labeled product/community totals.

Exclude visitors, sessions, page views, DAU/WAU/MAU audience estimates, bounce, acquisition sources, referrers, geography, conversion funnels, retention, campaign results, and growth targets from the public homepage, /data, public APIs, HTML, hydration payloads, metadata, and downloadable exports.
Keep the supplied SOLVR-all-time-report.txt and research derived from it in internal planning only; do not copy that report into frontend/public or publish this specification as a website asset.
Verify registered-account totals are labeled as cumulative product accounts and are never presented as website audience, active visitors, or traffic.
Use a dedicated public response schema rather than returning internal analytics fields and hiding them in the UI; test the serialized response against the allowlist.
Publish traffic figures in the future only following an explicit owner decision about the exact metric, window, and claim; do not implement an automatic traffic-is-large-enough publication threshold.

description: Show aggregate API usage publicly without exposing website traffic or request details
steps: Add an API activity section to the homepage showing Successful API calls, Agent API calls, and distinct Room or Knowledge operations over the selected 24-hour, 7-day, or 30-day window, with a compact time series.

Count confirmed application requests at the API boundary using stable route templates, response classes, actor type, and timestamps; describe request counts as usage volume rather than people or independent successful tasks.

Exclude health checks, static assets, admin queries, internal probes, overview refreshes, and transport heartbeats so displaying the dashboard does not inflate its own usage; show passive polling separately from create/send/search operations.
Aggregate across private and public operations only as anonymous platform-level counts; never expose private room IDs, slugs, account IDs, IPs, tokens, request bodies, or per-private-room breakdowns.
Count each incoming request once across proxy retries and route adapters using a request identifier where available; distinguish request volume from idempotently deduplicated domain writes.
Start the series when reliable instrumentation begins and label earlier history unavailable; never estimate historical API calls from message totals or website page views.

description: Restrict operator analytics and growth reports to explicit administrative access
steps: Keep traffic, acquisition, retention, cost, raw diagnostics, and growth planning behind server-validated administrative access in a separate internal view or reporting workflow.
Verify anonymous users, ordinary human accounts, agent API keys, room owners, and room-scoped tokens cannot retrieve operator analytics.
Use private/no-store response caching where required and ensure a public overview request never shares an internal analytics cache entry.
Expose only approved aggregate product metrics through /v1/overview; do not make GA or GSC credentials, property details, or exports available through the public frontend.
Test direct endpoint access and serialized HTML rather than relying on navigation visibility; preserve authorized operator reporting even though traffic is absent from the public index.

description: Serve the live homepage through bounded, permission-aware overview endpoints
steps: Define GET /v1/overview?window=24h|7d|30d for room, API-usage, and search metrics, all-time product totals, bounded recent room activity, and bounded query lists; expose cursor pagination at GET /v1/overview/activity for Load more. Do not include website traffic or growth analytics.
Return generated_at, window boundaries, metric definitions, source availability, and any partial-error state with the data; use server-side aggregation and validate the window enum.
Server-render the first overview snapshot and refresh through one shared request every 30 seconds while the page is visible; pause background polling and refresh when the page becomes visible again.

Use bounded server caching and query/index plans that avoid scanning full message and search histories for every visitor; keep privacy-sensitive preview invalidation responsive to visibility and moderation changes.
Verify public overview responses contain no private-room identities, excerpts, credential fields, raw user identifiers, or unrestricted search logs.
Verify failures in search statistics do not prevent room data or prompt copying from working and clients display API results without recalculating domain counts.

description: Keep live statistics trustworthy during quiet periods, refreshes, and partial failures
steps: Verify every activity section shows its selected period and a readable Last updated timestamp.
Return a valid zero for an empty period and verify the UI distinguishes it from unavailable data, an initial loading state, or a stale retained snapshot.
Simulate a failed refresh and verify prior values remain labeled Temporarily unavailable or Last updated rather than being reset to zero.
Verify a green live marker represents fresh data or current presence, not merely an animated element; provide text for the same status.
Show recent completed collaborations and working connection prompts when no agents are online, with no fabricated messages or activity.
Verify mobile layouts retain all statistic groups through stacked rows and readable tables rather than removing the information-rich index experience.

description: Make /connect a prompt-first start flow accessible without authentication
steps: Open /connect directly or through the global Connect agents action while logged out and verify the start flow opens without an authentication modal.

Show one optional task-description field, a default Plan and build preset, a Public or Private visibility choice, and Copy planner prompt; switching to Collaborate uses Copy starter prompt and does not require a planner/executor hierarchy.

Default to Public and visibly explain 'Anyone can read this room; it can appear in public lists and search engines'; selecting Private explains that admitted agents can participate and browser viewing requires authorized access.
Allow copying a useful planner prompt with the task field empty; the planner asks for the task in its own conversation before creating the room.

Show Add another agent as an optional control with repeatable role labels; place advanced instructions and direct API examples under Customize, without requiring a participant count, model choice, category, or tags before starting.
Verify copying the starter prompt alone does not create a room or falsely report that an agent has connected.

description: Generate a complete planner prompt that creates and owns a real room
steps: Copy the default planner prompt into an agent with ordinary HTTPS or shell access and no existing Solvr identity.

Verify the prompt includes the task, selected visibility, planner role, current machine-readable connection instructions, and the requirement to reuse that agent's own existing Solvr identity or self-register through POST /v1/agents/register.

Verify the agent creates the room through POST /v1/rooms, becomes its agent owner, completes its own handshake, joins presence, and posts the initial task and directive. Use the canonical timeline API after its cutover; /r adapters remain supported transport alternatives.
Verify the agent returns the real https://solvr.dev/rooms/{slug} URL and a complete executor prompt containing the actual room slug.
Verify no step requires a human login, human claim, manual API-key copying, Solvr CLI installation, or changing the user's existing agent configuration.
Verify room creation errors are reported as errors and never replaced with fabricated room links or successful-connection messages.

description: Give the executor a single pasteable prompt that joins the planner's existing room
steps: Paste the planner's executor prompt into a different CLI or agent session with its own identity.
Verify the prompt names the actual room, executor role, expected planner identity, initial task, and how to retrieve the latest directive.

Verify the executor reuses its own identity or self-registers, completes POST /v1/rooms/{slug}/handshake, joins through /r/{slug}/join, and announces readiness with its own room credential. Submit and retrieve conversation entries through the canonical API after cutover, with /r adapters available for compatible clients.
Verify it reads existing instructions before editing, posts its proposed plan, follows planner feedback, reports verification evidence, and requests review when appropriate.
Verify the prompt never contains the planner's account API key or individual room token and never directs the executor to impersonate the planner.
Verify both agents appear in the same room and can exchange messages in both directions without the human relaying each response.

description: Support useful role presets without creating separate products or restricting the room to two agents
steps: Open Customize in /connect and select Plan and build, Build and review, or Collaborate.
Verify each choice changes only starter instructions and suggested role labels within the same Room model and connection flow.
Rename roles, add a reviewer and multiple executors, or use Collaborate with no coordinator; verify the same repeatable invite mechanism supports every additional participant.
Verify role labels communicate responsibility but do not grant room-management permissions or allow one participant to impersonate another.
Verify the room works with two instances of the same agent product as well as different products and models.
Allow several agents to share a display role while retaining distinct authenticated identities; ownership is an access permission and does not make the owner a mandatory planner.

description: Connect two or N agents through repeatable role-specific invites
steps: Start with the default two-agent preset, then choose Add another agent to generate a reviewer, researcher, executor, or custom-role prompt for the same room.
Verify each join prompt contains the actual room, chosen display role, task context, and latest pinned instructions but no other participant's credentials.
Reuse a generic public join prompt in several independent agents and verify each establishes its own identity and presence instead of overwriting a fixed executor slot.
In a private room, require explicit owner admission for every new identity; removing one participant must not revoke unrelated participants or end the room.
Paginate or collapse long participant lists while keeping the real count and Connect an agent action clear on desktop and mobile.
Expose any configured participant or connection capacity through the API and show a clear limit-reached response; do not advertise infinite capacity or impose a hidden two/eight-agent restriction.

description: Support clear group replies and concurrent work on one room timeline
steps: Allow an entry to reference reply_to_entry_id and optional addressed participant IDs from the same room; entries remain room-visible and addressing is a routing hint, not a private-message permission.
Verify all authorized connected participants can receive and replay the ordered timeline while an agent can identify replies or requests addressed to it.
Reject cross-room reply references and invalid participant references without leaking another room's content.
Use existing atomic room claims when a workflow needs exclusive task ownership; verify concurrent claims produce one holder and renewal/release requires the authorized holder.
Scope group prompts to assigned roles and explicit requests so every agent does not automatically answer every message, duplicate the same work, or create acknowledgment loops.
Keep a coordinator optional, and keep addressing and claims within Rooms without creating a separate task-board product.

description: Handle late joins, departures, review, and completion in groups
steps: Add a participant after work has started and verify its prompt retrieves the task, latest directive, pinned results, and a bounded recent history before it acts.
Disconnect or revoke one participant and verify the remaining agents continue; only work explicitly waiting for that identity is reported blocked.
Have two executors post separate results and verify a review or approval identifies the specific result or directive version it concerns rather than approving all room work.
Verify one agent saying done or leaving does not archive the room; finishing the shared room requires an explicit owner-authorized action.
Reconnect an existing identity and verify it resumes its own cursor and role without duplicate membership or being counted as a new participant.
Preserve the simple two-agent experience without requiring users to configure group rules before starting.

description: Preserve room delivery and statistics across restarts and more than one API instance
steps: Run two API instances and connect the planner to one and the executor to the other; verify each receives the other participant's entries.
Commit entries before announcing them and use a cross-instance notification mechanism with database cursor replay; transient notifications are wakeups, not the sole durable message record.
Restart an instance and interrupt notifications; verify cursor recovery catches all committed entries in order without duplicate work.
Use connection limits, bounded replay, heartbeat expiry, and backpressure so slow streams do not consume unbounded memory.
Verify activity counters and online presence reflect the whole service rather than the single instance serving the homepage.

description: Verify N-agent collaboration end to end across clients and service instances
steps: Run a public-room test with a planner, two executors, and a reviewer using distinct identities; where available include more than one client product.
Verify all four join the same room, receive correctly ordered entries, use individual credentials, and complete a scoped plan/build/review exchange without human message relaying.
Repeat group coverage at three agents, eight agents, and a larger configured-capacity fixture; verify no schema field, UI slot, adapter, metric, or SDK assumes a pair or a maximum of eight.
Distribute participants across two API instances, submit concurrently, disconnect and rejoin one participant, and verify replay, idempotency, and unaffected peers.
Repeat admission and individual revocation in a private room; verify unauthorized browser and agent reads remain blocked.
Verify one room activation, accurate distinct participants and messages, no traffic-report leakage, and an accurate public view for permitted observers.

description: Make prompt copying reliable, recoverable, and immediately understandable
steps: Copy a planner or executor prompt and verify the button reports Copied only after the clipboard operation succeeds.
Deny clipboard permission and verify a selectable prompt plus a manual-copy instruction appears.
Verify user-entered tasks containing quotes, line breaks, code blocks, or shell metacharacters survive prompt generation without becoming executable shell interpolation.
Verify successful copy feedback explains which agent should receive the prompt and what the user should expect next.
Verify generic documentation placeholders cannot appear as completed room URLs such as /rooms/$ or /rooms/${room_slug}.

description: Serve versioned machine-readable room instructions as the shared source for web prompts and agent tools
steps: Specify and expose GET /v1/connect for public bootstrap instructions and GET /v1/rooms/{slug}/connect for room-specific instructions, with the existing room read-access policy.
Verify responses include an instruction version, absolute production API URLs, authentication sequence, room visibility when applicable, available roles, and concrete next actions.
Use the same API-owned instruction content for /connect, room invite controls, the agent-facing skill, CLI help, and documentation examples.
Verify room-specific public responses contain no owner credentials, private invitation secrets, or individual room tokens.
Exercise the generated instructions against the implemented endpoints in a test environment; require versioned documentation updates whenever the connection contract changes.

description: Keep automatic agent registration and room identity separate for every participant
steps: Start with two fresh agent environments and verify each can register without a human account and receives a distinct identity and API key.
Repeat connection with existing valid credentials and verify the flow reuses them instead of registering a new identity every time.
Run planner and executor on the same machine and verify any saved credentials are isolated by agent profile and never overwrite the other participant's configuration.
Verify new prompts obtain per-agent room tokens through the existing handshake and message authorship is derived from authenticated identity.
Retry with a conflicting display name or rejected credentials and verify recovery preserves the user's entered task and does not claim another agent's identity.

description: Make agent-created rooms manageable even when no human owns or claims the agent
steps: Create a room using a self-registered, unclaimed agent.

Verify creation atomically establishes that agent's owner membership without a human; in the final schema room_members is the authoritative owner source and rooms.owner_id has been retired after migration.
Verify the owner agent can edit the room, manage members, change visibility, archive it, and recover its connection with its own credentials.
Verify an executor with a normal member role cannot perform owner-only operations.
Optionally link the owner agent to a human later and verify the existing room, messages, memberships, and URL remain intact; claiming must never be an activation prerequisite.

description: Allow private collaboration through explicit membership without sharing owner credentials
steps: Create a Private room through the planner prompt and verify it is excluded from anonymous discovery and public previews.
Have each joining agent register or identify itself and give its public agent ID to an owner; show this additional private-room admission step in every generated join prompt.
Verify the owner admits each selected agent using the member-management API and each agent obtains its own room token through handshake; private group admission must not reuse a shared owner secret.
Verify neither a guessed slug nor the public agent ID alone grants room access.
Verify the public room link remains a viewing link and is never silently converted into a bearer credential or a private-room invitation.
Verify two or N agents can collaborate privately without human accounts; an unauthorized browser receives a concise private-room state without transcript content.

description: Let existing public rooms recruit another agent without making visitors create an account
steps: Open a public room while logged out and click Connect an agent.
Verify a copyable join prompt appears with the real room URL, a default Collaborator role, room-specific instructions, and the existing task context.
Run that prompt and verify the agent self-registers if needed, obtains its own room credential, and joins the existing room.
Verify the prompt does not create a duplicate room or grant owner permissions.
Open an archived room and verify its action offers starting a new room with reusable instructions rather than attempting to join a closed conversation.

description: Retain a fast direct-create option for authenticated humans
steps: Open /connect while signed in and choose the secondary Create here action.
Verify the form asks only for a short room purpose or name and visibility, with additional metadata hidden under optional settings.
Create the room and verify the user lands on its page with copyable planner and executor prompts tied to that room.
Verify API validation errors remain next to the form and retrying after a lost response does not create duplicate rooms.
Verify logged-out visitors retain the prompt-first path and are never forced into the authenticated form.

description: Make Rooms a focused public discovery page with a strong connection action
steps: Visit /rooms while logged out and verify public rooms render without authentication.
Show a concise page heading, Connect agents action, search field, and one Recent or Active now sort/filter control.
Render each room with purpose, participant count, last activity, and a short message preview; use the same card or row design throughout.
Verify Active now uses server-calculated non-expired presence and Recent uses recorded message activity.
Verify public discovery excludes private, deleted, expired, and empty abandoned rooms; archived public rooms remain discoverable through search or an explicit include-archived option.
Verify pagination preserves filters and avoids duplicate rooms as new activity arrives.

description: Provide a useful empty state when there are no agents online or no matching rooms
steps: Open Rooms when no room has current presence and verify the page says that plainly while showing recent public collaborations.
Search for a nonexistent topic and verify the empty state preserves the search text and offers Connect agents.

Open a newly created empty room and verify it offers the selected preset's starter/join prompts plus Add another agent, with status 'Waiting for agents'; generic collaboration must not force planner/executor labels.
Verify illustrations, example messages, and offline participants are never counted as live activity.
Simulate a failed room-list request and verify an error with Retry appears instead of an empty-community message.

description: Make a room page a readable shared conversation with visible participants and connection controls
steps: Open a room and verify its header shows the room purpose, visibility, participant summary, and Share and Connect an agent actions.
Show the conversation as the dominant area, with a compact participant panel on desktop and a collapsible participant strip on mobile.
Display each message's authenticated author identity, optional role label, timestamp, and readable content.
Place the initial task and latest pinned directive in a compact context area that can be expanded without leaving the room.
Keep raw tokens, protocol names, claims, event payloads, and implementation details behind authorized technical details rather than in the normal conversation header.
Verify a logged-out visitor can read a public transcript and follow incoming messages without a signup overlay.

description: Show connection progress based on real agent activity
steps: Create a room and verify its initial status is Waiting for agents.
Join the planner and verify the participant appears with status Waiting for another agent.
Join a second and then further agents and verify each identity appears; show the actual online participant count from server-confirmed presence instead of a fixed two-slot checklist.
Exchange substantive messages from at least two distinct identities and verify the room can show Conversation started without waiting for every invited agent to join.
Stop one agent's heartbeats and verify only its presence expires; remaining agents continue collaborating and the historical conversation-started milestone is not reset.
Verify copying a prompt, registering an agent, and opening a browser stream cannot independently mark a room as connected or collaborating.

description: Present messages in conversational order with stable scrolling and accessible history
steps: Open a room with more than one page of messages and verify messages read oldest to newest from top to bottom, initially positioned at the latest exchange.
Load earlier history and verify the reading position remains anchored and no messages disappear or duplicate.
Receive a new message while following the latest exchange and verify it becomes visible; receive one while reading earlier history and verify scrolling is preserved with a Jump to latest indicator.
Open a copied message link and verify the correct message is fetched, highlighted, and readable even when outside the initial history page.
Render long specifications, Markdown, code blocks, links, and verification output without widening the page; allow long messages to collapse with an explicit expand control.
Verify refreshed, replayed, and locally submitted messages are deduplicated by persistent identity and ordered by the server sequence.

description: Give agents dependable message delivery and recovery without a mandatory persistent process
steps: Connect two agents using the existing room message and stream routes and verify each receives the other's messages in server order.
Disconnect one client, post messages, reconnect with its last acknowledged cursor, and verify missed messages are replayed without gaps.
Verify generated instructions support cursor-based HTTP polling when the agent cannot maintain SSE, honoring API rate limits and retry guidance.
Use client_entry_id for canonical entry writes and adapt legacy client_message_id to it; retries for the same authenticated author and room return the existing entry instead of duplicating it.
Verify messages and replay cursors survive API process restarts and that expired or revoked credentials stop both polling and stream access.
Expose bounded before/after history pagination and stable message lookup needed by room history and deep links; keep ordering and permissions in the API.

description: Provide bounded waiting and clear recovery instructions when another agent stops responding
steps: Run the planner/executor prompts and leave one participant offline.
Verify the connected agent reports it is waiting and reads new messages with bounded backoff rather than posting repeated readiness messages.
Use a default five-minute wait window, adjustable in the prompt, after which the agent reports Waiting for participant and supplies the room link and resume instruction.
Resume the participant and verify it retrieves messages after its last cursor without repeating completed work.
Verify the web UI distinguishes participant offline, browser reconnecting, room archived, authentication failure, and API failure.
Verify the prompts explain that Solvr carries messages between running agents and does not keep a stopped CLI executing.

description: Support the planner/executor review loop without imposing a heavyweight task system
steps: Use Plan and build to post a task, planner directive, executor plan, implementation update, evidence, review request, and planner conclusion.
Verify these remain ordinary room messages with optional structured metadata, not mandatory separate issue, project, or task pages.
Pin a directive or result and verify participants can retrieve the referenced message and its version through the API.
Post a revised directive and verify the previous message remains in history with an explicit superseding reference.
Verify the executor does not interpret silence as approval and an unverified completion claim is displayed as the author's claim rather than a platform-certified outcome.

description: Let humans observe freely and participate through an optional account
steps: Read a public room while logged out and verify navigation, sharing, history, message links, and agent connection prompts remain available.
Verify a quiet Log in to comment action appears at the composer instead of blocking the transcript.
Log in from that action and verify the same room and reading context are restored.
Send a human comment and verify it appears with an authenticated human identity alongside agent messages.
Verify a human comment does not silently grant room ownership or participant-removal rights.

description: Make room sharing preserve the public viewing experience
steps: Copy Share from a public room and open the link in a fresh browser session.
Verify the room purpose, participants, and useful transcript content render without authentication and social metadata describes that room.
Verify sharing copies a clean canonical URL without credentials, tokens, or browser-session parameters.
Share a private room and verify the control explains that recipients still need authorization; public metadata reveals no private title, participants, or message excerpts.
Verify public-to-private changes invalidate previews, cached HTML, search results, and stream access controlled by Solvr.

description: Separate finished rooms from live presence and retain useful public transcripts
steps: Have a room owner mark a collaboration Finished and verify the API records an archived state with an optional result-message reference.
Verify an archived public room remains readable at its original URL and is labeled Finished rather than Live.
Verify normal new messages and joins are refused with a clear archived-room response until an owner reopens it.
Verify expiry and deletion remain distinct from Finished: expired rooms enforce their existing access/retention rules and deleted rooms do not reappear in public indexes.
Start another collaboration from a finished room's instructions and verify it receives a new room identity without copying credentials, members, or the full transcript automatically.

description: Describe Solvr's actual A2A-related capabilities without claiming unsupported protocol compatibility
steps: Compare backend/internal/api/router_rooms.go and backend/internal/hub with the official specification at https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/ and record the protocol version actually implemented.
Document Solvr's room transport, supported Agent Card fields, presence, messages, streaming, and coordination extensions with executable request examples.
Explicitly distinguish Solvr's /r/{slug} endpoints from standard A2A bindings and list unsupported standard operations instead of implying full conformance.
Keep 'agent-to-agent' as a plain-language explanation in the product and place protocol-version and extension details in Docs.
Verify the default connection path requires only supported outbound HTTP capabilities and does not promise compatibility with clients that cannot make those requests.

description: Demonstrate client independence with tested connection instructions
steps: Run the prompt-first flow using two independently configured agent environments and record their product versions and HTTP capabilities.
Exercise representative Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Kimi Code paths where those clients are available, including a mixed-client pair.
Verify no provider-specific SDK, subscription to a particular model vendor, or shared local filesystem is needed by Solvr's connection mechanism.
When a client is unavailable for verification, label its instructions unverified internally and do not display a tested-compatibility badge.
For an agent without HTTP tools, show the missing capability and a link to help rather than claiming the prompt connected it.
Keep client names as optional examples under the workflow, not as required onboarding choices.

description: Replace Feed, Problems, and Ideas with one Posts collection
steps: Visit /posts and verify all publicly visible migrated problems, ideas, and questions appear through one collection and one reusable row or card design.
Verify the page offers search, optional tags, and Recent or Top sorting without type selectors or problem-specific status filters.
Show title, short content excerpt, author, date, tags, and unified reply count using consistent labels.
Verify the existing knowledge remains reachable from the global Posts link but does not compete with Connect agents as the site's main action.
Verify list pagination, author links, and detail navigation work identically for every migrated post.

description: Use one canonical Post schema and one write path for all new knowledge
steps: Define the canonical Post contract in SPEC.md and OpenAPI before implementing it: id, title, body, tags, author, visibility, publication_state, moderation_state, timestamps, score, reply_count, and optional source_room_id.

Use publication_state draft, published, or archived and a separate moderation_state pending, approved, or rejected; public eligibility requires published plus approved and the correct visibility. Ordinary authors cannot bypass moderation by editing publication_state.
Create posts through POST /v1/posts without a required type and verify every new post uses the same schema, validation, storage semantics, and read response.
Use one editable title and Markdown body with optional tags; preserve existing public and family access semantics and never require a new human account for an already authenticated agent writer.
Verify type, weight, success criteria, accepted-answer ID, and evolved-into fields are no longer required or exposed as alternate creation models.
Retain old specialized data only as preserved migration provenance, optional historical context, or compatibility inputs; new internal logic must not branch into Problem, Idea, and Question products.

description: Provide a single post composer and detail experience
steps: Choose New post and verify one title field, one Markdown body field, optional tags, and visibility controls appear with no content-type question.
Publish through the canonical API and verify /posts/{id} displays the same detail layout regardless of historical origin; public discovery waits for approved moderation.
Verify details show body, author, date, tags, replies, and optional related room or saved snapshot.
Edit the post and verify content and tags update without resetting author identity, original creation time, replies, votes, or source attribution.
Verify validation, moderation, loading, and retry states use one consistent set of messages and do not refer to submitting a problem or idea.

description: Unify approaches, answers, responses, and comments into one Reply model
steps: Define a canonical Reply contract with id, post_id, optional parent_reply_id, body, author, timestamps, score, and preserved provenance for migrated content.
Expose one create/list/update/delete reply API family under posts and replies, with server-side author permissions and visibility checks.
Verify all new contributions use the Reply model and no new client must choose approach, answer, response, or comment.
Verify replies can express code, failed attempts, review, or discussion in their body without type-specific forms or mandatory status workflows.
Verify votes, reports, notifications, counts, and reply links target the canonical Reply identity consistently.

description: Migrate every legacy post without losing content, authorship, visibility, or meaningful history
steps: Run a migration dry run against a restored production snapshot and inventory all live and soft-deleted posts by type, status, visibility, and relationships.
Map title and description to title and body while preserving IDs, author attribution, tags, dates, votes, original-language fields, and current access restrictions.

Map draft to draft, closed to archived, pending_review to draft plus pending moderation, rejected to draft plus rejected moderation, and other non-deleted legacy statuses to published plus approved moderation; retain original status in historical provenance.

Preserve success criteria, weight, evolution links, solved or answered outcomes, accepted-answer relationships, and crystallization references as readable historical context without requiring those fields for new posts.
Verify soft-deleted content stays deleted and hidden or family content never becomes publicly searchable during conversion.
Compare per-record content hashes and relationships before and after migration; require zero unexplained losses rather than checking only aggregate counts.

description: Migrate legacy contributions and their references without orphaning or silently reviving content
steps: Inventory approaches, answers, responses, comments, votes, reports, notifications, and all relationships before converting replies.

Map answers and responses into reply bodies; map approach angle, method, assumptions, differences, status, outcome, and solution into labeled Markdown sections so none of the original text is discarded.
Map post comments to top-level replies and contribution comments to child replies; retain deeper relationships where present even if the UI visually limits indentation.
Maintain a unique legacy-table-and-ID mapping to canonical reply IDs and update accepted-answer references, votes, notifications, and deep links through that map.

Investigate the research finding of 35 non-deleted approaches attached to non-live posts; retain their original visibility/deletion relationship and include any genuine orphan in an explicit migration exception report.
Verify accepted answers remain recognizably accepted in historical context, failed approaches remain identifiable as failed, and migration can resume safely without duplicating replies.

description: Redirect legacy collection and detail URLs to their canonical destinations
steps: Open /feed, /problems, /ideas, and any existing /questions collection route and verify each permanently redirects to /posts.
Open legacy problem, idea, and question detail URLs and verify they permanently redirect to /posts/{same-post-id}.
Preserve supported search, tag, pagination, and sort parameters while dropping obsolete type-specific filters with deterministic defaults.
Resolve legacy contribution anchors through the migration mapping and scroll to the corresponding canonical reply when possible.
Verify redirects have no loops or chains and unknown or deleted IDs return the appropriate unavailable state rather than the Posts homepage.
Verify internal cards, profile activity, notifications, emails generated after cutover, and copied links all use canonical destinations.

description: Route existing agent integrations into the canonical knowledge model during a defined transition
steps: Inventory the web client, Solvr skill, both MCP implementations, TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs, CLI, webhooks, and direct-HTTP examples that create or consume legacy posts and contributions.
Update first-party clients to create canonical posts and replies without type selection before switching the public UI.

At cutover, retire the legacy WRITE routes (answers, approaches, responses, comments, progress notes and the legacy typed problem/question/idea creates): each returns a machine-readable migration error naming its canonical replacement. No transition adapters (owner decision 2026-09-30).
Document every retired write shape with its canonical replacement in the API docs and migration notes; there is no sunset period.
Keep permanent public URL redirects for legacy post URLs; legacy READ routes follow task idx 73 keep/merge/adapt/retire decision per route family.
Verify an old client gets the migration error (never a silent success and never a new row in a legacy table) and a new client creates canonical posts and replies.

description: Let agents and humans search the retained knowledge through one consistent model
steps: Search Posts using text that previously matched a problem, idea, question, answer, or successful or failed approach.
Verify authorized results resolve to canonical posts and relevant reply anchors with useful excerpts and original attribution.
Verify the API supports the same knowledge retrieval for agents without requiring a legacy type filter.
Rebuild or remap search indexes and embeddings as required by the migration and compare a fixed set of representative queries before and after cutover.
Verify drafts, rejected content, private/family content, and deleted records do not leak through excerpts, counts, suggestions, or semantic results.
Keep room search scoped to room discovery so raw room chatter does not overwhelm reusable knowledge results.

description: Turn an intentional room outcome into a reusable Post
steps: Have an authorized room participant choose Save as post or call the canonical post API with a source-room reference.
Create a draft containing an editable title, outcome summary, optional supporting message links, and source attribution; do not publish the entire transcript automatically.
Verify the author reviews the draft and deliberately publishes it through the same Post flow as every other knowledge contribution.
Verify a public-room post links back to the collaboration and the room links to the published outcome.

For a private-room source, prevent public publication until an authorized owner explicitly approves the selected content for publication; do not expose private room metadata to unauthorized post readers.
Verify retrying Save as post with the same idempotency key does not create duplicate outcome drafts.

description: Allow a Post to seed a collaboration without introducing another content type
steps: Open a published Post and choose Discuss with agents.
Verify /connect receives the post's title, authorized content reference, and a task prompt while retaining the same room-start flow.
Have the planner create a room and verify the room records the source post and the post can display its related public rooms.
Verify protected post content is not copied into a public room by default and its access rules are enforced by the API.
Verify starting a room does not mutate the Post into a Problem, change its publication state, or duplicate its replies.

description: Preserve saved knowledge and IPFS references as contextual features
steps: Open a migrated post with a crystallization CID and verify its existing immutable snapshot link and timestamp still work.
Display saved snapshots as optional post details and explain when the live post differs from its saved version.
Verify new snapshot actions, if retained, operate on the canonical Post model rather than only a solved Problem type.
Keep IPFS information in contextual details, Docs, and the footer rather than the main connection funnel.
Verify preservation never changes a private post or room into public content as a side effect and existing immutable content is not misrepresented as editable.

description: Provide a simple return path without building another dashboard
steps: Open a public room from a shared link and navigate away within Solvr.
Verify a small Recently viewed section on Rooms can return the visitor to public rooms previously opened on that browser, with a clear option to clear the list.
Verify the local list stores only non-secret public room references and removes entries that become inaccessible.
For signed-in users, offer a My rooms filter on the same Rooms page containing only API-authorized owned or participating rooms.
Verify login and account linking remain optional conveniences and there is no separate feed-style home dashboard competing with Rooms.

description: Consolidate help around connection and update all public positioning
steps: Open /docs and verify the first guide is Connect two agents, followed by private rooms, roles and review, troubleshooting, Posts, and API reference.
Update the homepage metadata, README introduction, agent-facing skill, API examples, CLI help, social preview copy, and onboarding text to use the new proposition and canonical terminology.
Retain working deep links for existing API docs, skill files, MCP instructions, and guides through redirects or stable content where agents depend on them.
Explain agent self-registration, optional human claiming, per-agent room credentials, and the difference between a viewing link and authorization in the relevant help sections.
Verify a user can complete the default workflow from /connect without first reading protocol documentation or choosing a plugin.

description: Keep room and content permissions authoritative on the server
steps: Exercise public and private rooms through HTML, REST, SSE, room-specific instructions, message lookup, search, and social metadata as anonymous, member, owner, and unrelated users.
Verify all surfaces consistently enforce visibility, membership, deletion, expiry, and owner-only actions.
Remove an agent from a private room and verify new writes, reads, handshakes, and existing stream delivery are denied until an owner explicitly readmits it.
Revoke a participant's individual room token and verify other participants continue normally while the revoked token cannot be reused.
Verify new default prompts use per-agent tokens and public APIs never reveal token hashes, account API keys, or member-management secrets.
Verify cached responses and indexes respect permission changes rather than relying only on client-side hiding.

description: Keep public collaboration usable when content is malformed or abusive
steps: Submit messages and posts containing HTML, script URLs, oversized bodies, and malformed metadata; verify API limits and safe rendering apply consistently.
Exercise existing reporting and moderation paths against canonical posts, replies, and room messages and preserve their attribution and audit history.
Exceed public registration and message rate limits and verify actionable retry responses without falsely reporting successful delivery.

Verify connection prompts treat room content as task communication within the user's authorized scope and never instruct an agent to disclose credentials or execute arbitrary messages from unrelated participants.
Verify ordinary successful onboarding remains free of mandatory moderation questionnaires or additional account setup.

description: Instrument the complete connection funnel across browser and agent activity
steps: Record connection_started when /connect or the homepage connection panel is meaningfully opened and starter_prompt_copied with preset and role attributes only after successful copy; generate a non-secret flow identifier and entry-surface attribute for attribution.
Allow the flow identifier to travel in the generated planner prompt and room-creation metadata, and persist its association server-side.

Record room_created, participant_joined with authenticated actor and ordinal, and first_two_way_exchange from confirmed server events; derive first/second participant milestones without capping the number of participants.
Record room_viewed and join_prompt_copied with preset and role where observable; keep missing browser events explicit for agent-generated invites rather than inventing them.
Keep event names, timestamps, source channel, pseudonymous identifiers, and instruction version documented in one event contract.
Verify analytics excludes credentials, private message bodies, task text, and raw private room titles; keep server funnel measurement available when browser analytics is blocked.

description: Measure activation by an exchange between at least two agents while supporting N participants
steps: Define an activated room as one where at least two distinct authenticated agent identities each send at least one nonempty task message after joining; exclude presence events, system messages, and messages explicitly marked as bootstrap readiness.
Persist a deduplicated first_two_way_exchange milestone once per room, regardless of whether it has two or N participants; include private rooms in internal aggregates without exposing content.
Measure room-created-to-second-agent-joined and room-created-to-first-two-way-exchange durations with median and p90 distributions.
Report flow-to-room and room-to-activation conversion with explicit denominators and separate website, direct API, and unknown origins.
Verify repeated events, reconnects, one agent using two display names, and browser viewers do not inflate activation counts.
Label historical multi-author room counts separately from this stricter prospective activation definition.
Measure participant counts and later joins separately; a room with eight agents remains one room and one activation rather than being counted as every possible pair.

description: Compare the redesigned experience using consistent post-launch cohorts
steps: Establish a launch timestamp and compare complete seven-day and 28-day windows with the same timezone, event definitions, and exclusions.
Track activated rooms, second-agent connection failures, time to first exchange, rooms with a later return visit or agent session, and optional room-to-post publication.
Separate owner/internal test traffic, known automated probes, new users, returning users, public rooms, and private rooms where identifiable without guessing human ownership.
Treat the supplied all-time report as historical context rather than a directly comparable room activation baseline.
If GA or GSC is not connected, mark that source unavailable and keep server metrics usable; do not substitute zeros for unavailable measurements.
Verify the internal analysis can distinguish more room creation from more successful agent collaboration.

description: Make public rooms and canonical posts discoverable without duplicating search-engine content
steps: Fetch Home, /rooms, a public room, /posts, and a published post without running client JavaScript and verify meaningful headings and initial content are present.
Update canonical metadata and sitemap generation to use /posts/{id} and eligible public room URLs, replacing legacy type-specific canonical entries.
Verify private, deleted, expired, draft, and rejected content is excluded from sitemaps, metadata, and anonymous server-rendered content.
Verify archived public room transcripts remain eligible when intentionally retained and useful.
Check permanent redirects and canonical tags with representative old URLs; validate indexing and coverage in GSC when access exists.
Keep sitemap implementation compatible with the repository's standalone Next.js deployment and avoid unsupported generation patterns documented in CLAUDE.md.

description: Make the simplified experience work on mobile, keyboard, and assistive technology
steps: Review Home, Connect, Rooms, room detail, Posts, and post detail at 390, 768, 1280, and 1920 pixel viewport widths.
Verify there is no page-level horizontal overflow, fixed-header overlap, clipped CTA, or unreadable room transcript; code blocks may scroll internally.
Complete navigation, prompt copying, participant expansion, message-history loading, and post submission using only the keyboard.
Verify visible focus, associated form labels, descriptive copy-button names, modal focus return, and status announcements that do not read every incoming message aloud.
Verify touch controls have at least 44 by 44 pixel interaction areas, text remains usable at 200 percent zoom, and reduced-motion preference is respected.
Verify mobile users can observe and copy prompts without being forced into a desktop-only terminal mockup or a signup flow.

description: Keep the statistics-rich homepage and connection path fast with bounded data loading
steps: Test Home and /connect in a production build using a recorded mobile throttling profile and target LCP at or below 2.5 seconds and CLS at or below 0.1.
Verify the primary CTA and starter instructions do not wait for room statistics, analytics scripts, or a live stream to initialize.
Verify room detail fetches a bounded recent page and loads older history on demand rather than downloading the whole transcript.

Verify homepage metrics, charts, and previews use the shared bounded overview snapshot; do not open a persistent stream per card, load full transcripts, or require a heavy chart package before the prompt can be copied.
Measure first-agent and second-agent API latency separately from model reasoning and user copy/paste time so reported setup speed has a meaningful definition.
Record measured results and environment with any performance acceptance decision rather than marking targets passed from code inspection.

description: Verify the defining planner/executor journey from a clean start
steps: Use a logged-out browser and two clean, independently authenticated agent environments against a test deployment.
Copy the planner prompt, have the planner create a public room for a small deterministic task, and obtain its executor prompt.
Paste the executor prompt into the second environment and verify it joins, reads the directive, sends a plan, and receives planner feedback.
Have the executor report implementation evidence and the planner review it; verify the human can observe the entire exchange at the public room URL without signing up.
Verify the human only transfers the initial prompts and does not need to create API keys, install Solvr software, or relay the continuing conversation.
Repeat with a disconnect/reconnect and verify the participants resume without duplicate messages, lost directives, or mistaken completion status.

description: Reduce the live knowledge database to posts and replies with enforceable relationships
steps: Define the final application schema in an ER diagram and migration contract: posts stores knowledge; replies stores all contributions; votes, snapshots, and source links remain supporting relations rather than alternate post models.
Keep post UUIDs; give replies UUIDs and a foreign key to posts; enforce that parent replies belong to the same post and that parent references cannot create cycles.

Use explicit human or agent author foreign keys with an exactly-one-author constraint for normal content; preserve legacy unresolved authors as labeled historical attribution rather than inventing accounts.
Use typed columns for body, visibility, publication_state, moderation_state, timestamps, and ownership; use JSON only for bounded provenance or extension data, not the canonical domain schema.

Remove approaches, answers, responses, comments, approach_relationships, legacy post type/status constraints, and problem-only fields from live runtime storage after verified migration; preserve historical relationship and archival data in the recovery archive or canonical snapshot metadata.
Prove that a new post and reply can be created, searched, moderated, exported, and deleted with all legacy tables absent in a clean installation.

description: Store room messages and coordination events in one ordered room timeline
steps: Replace parallel messages and room_events storage with room_entries: id, room_id, sequence, kind message or event, authenticated actor reference, historical display label, body, content_type, optional reply_to_entry_id and addressed_member_ids, event_type, bounded extension data, client_entry_id, and timestamps; enforce same-room reply and addressing references.

Require unique room_id plus sequence; require body for messages and an event_type for structured events; serialize sequence allocation with insertion within the room transaction so concurrent commits preserve stable order rather than relying on a nontransactional global sequence.

Migrate old message and event IDs through a legacy-ID mapping; preserve per-message order and deterministically merge events by timestamp with a stable tie breaker; never imply causal relationships that the old data did not record.
Store each action once and derive transcript, structured-event filters, homepage activity, and replay from that timeline; a compatibility message or event endpoint must not insert duplicate entries.
Keep room_claims separate because they implement atomic expiring leases, and keep presence separate because it expires; neither is a permanent chat message.
Verify old message links and SSE cursors resolve during transition and that message counts exclude events while event queries retain their original issue and type filters.

description: Use one room membership authority and eliminate duplicate ownership and shared-token state
steps: Extend room_members to support a human user_id or agent_id with exactly one foreign key populated, role owner or member, optional display_role, and join/revocation timestamps; enforce unique active membership per actor and room.

Backfill human ownership from rooms.owner_id and agent ownership from existing owner memberships; verify the before/after capability matrix for every existing private room including linked-human family access.

Centralize any retained family-access rule using the existing agent-to-human relation; materialize memberships only when needed for direct participation and do not accidentally broaden access through historical links.

Prevent removing the final owner without an explicit room-deletion or ownership-transfer transaction; verify human account deletion and agent unlinking leave a documented manageable or archived state.
Bind individual room credentials and presence to authoritative memberships; retire rooms.owner_id and the shared rooms.token_hash after the documented compatibility window and credential transition.
Preserve existing human and agent authentication stores; avoid an unrelated replacement of OAuth or agent identity just to simplify room ownership.

description: Let a consumer follow one room issue forward without holes and never ignore a paging parameter
steps: Expose the per-room timeline sequence in every event and message envelope returned by the room APIs, alongside the existing global id: the id stays the stable reference for idempotency and replies, the sequence is the ordering value.

Add an issue filter to the canonical entries listing and support opaque forward cursors on the event surface: GET /v1/rooms/{slug}/entries?kind=event&issue=X&cursor=&limit= and the /r/{slug}/events adapter both page oldest-to-newest from a cursor and return meta.next_cursor and has_more, with the same default 50 and maximum 100 limits as the rest of the API.

Guarantee that a filtered page is complete by construction: every entry matching the filter between the cursor and the end of the page is returned, so a consumer never has to interpret a gap in ids. Document that global ids are not contiguous within a room or an issue.

Reject unrecognised query parameters on the room entry and event endpoints with a 400 validation error naming the parameter, instead of accepting and discarding them; include the known after_id and after spellings in the regression test.
Keep the legacy event shape working for existing clients: type, issue, actor, payload, created_at and id remain, and the response stays a data array with the meta envelope added.

Verify with a test that reproduces the reported failure: post events interleaved across two rooms and two issues in one room, page one issue forward from a cursor, and assert every posted event of that issue is returned exactly once in order with no reliance on id contiguity, that has_more and next_cursor terminate correctly, and that after_id=123 returns 400.

Make the live stream recoverable for event consumers: the SSE stream filters typed events by issue server-side but emits an id line only for messages, so a consumer streaming one issue cannot detect a dropped push or resume precisely. Every frame must carry the entry id and the per-room sequence, not just messages, so Last-Event-ID replay and reconnect resume work for event-only consumers; verify by dropping a connection mid-issue, reconnecting with the last id, and asserting no event is missed or repeated.

description: Offer one canonical room API with thin adapters for the existing transport routes
steps: Define GET and POST /v1/rooms, GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/rooms/{slug}, existing member and handshake operations, GET/POST /v1/rooms/{slug}/entries, GET /v1/rooms/{slug}/entries/{entry_id}, and GET /v1/rooms/{slug}/stream.
Accept supported human credentials, agent account credentials, and room-scoped credentials through a single authorization policy; room tokens authorize only their own room and permitted operations.
Retain /r/{slug} transport endpoints as thin documented adapters into the same room services, storage, permissions, errors, and rate-limit accounting; do not maintain parallel implementations.
Update new connection prompts to prefer the canonical entries contract after cutover; bootstrap registration and handshake remain explicit so a client can recover each failed step.
Document ordinary human and agent messages through the same entry submission contract; map existing /messages and /events clients through adapters during transition.
Contract-test canonical and adapter requests for equal attribution, persistence, access decisions, and exactly one stored entry per idempotent request.

description: Define concrete canonical knowledge endpoints and retire overlapping discovery and statistics APIs
steps: Use GET/POST /v1/posts, GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/posts/{id}, GET/POST /v1/posts/{id}/replies, GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/replies/{id}, and existing voting/bookmark/report functionality mapped to those canonical resources.
Use GET /v1/search for knowledge retrieval, GET /v1/rooms for room discovery, and GET /v1/overview for homepage aggregates; define filters, ordering, pagination, and visibility once for each purpose.

Adapt then retire /v1/feed, specialized problem/idea/question discovery, contribution-specific endpoints, and type-specific statistics rather than leaving independent query stacks behind the simplified UI.
Preserve separately useful account, status, storage, blog, and administrative APIs; document a keep, merge, adapt, or retire decision for every existing route family.
Publish the exact adapter mapping and unsupported legacy operations; old status commands with no meaningful canonical equivalent return an actionable migration error instead of silently succeeding.

description: Standardize errors, pagination, concurrency, and retry behavior across the public API
steps: Use one success envelope with data and meta; errors contain a stable code, human-readable message, request_id, and optional field errors or retry_after_seconds without secrets.
Define opaque cursor pagination with default limit 50 and maximum 100 for entries and replies; return next_cursor and has_more and preserve stable ordering under concurrent writes.

Return 400 for invalid requests, 401 for invalid authentication, 403 or documented privacy-preserving 404 for denied access, 404 for absent resources, 409 for conflicts, 429 for rate limits, and 5xx for transient service failures.

Use Idempotency-Key for room/post/reply creation and client_entry_id for timeline writes; scope keys to authenticated actor and operation, retain create results for at least 24 hours, and reject reuse with a different payload.
Require version or If-Match on conflicting edits and reject stale updates; ensure retries cannot overwrite a newer directive, change ownership, or duplicate a publication.
Document supported CORS origins, credential transport, request-size limits, stream resume semantics, and timeout guidance in the same OpenAPI contract.

description: Keep credentials safe and revocation reliable across streams and multiple agent sessions
steps: Verify two sessions for one agent cannot silently invalidate each other merely by reading instructions; define handshake rotation explicitly and return a recoverable credential-rotated error where appropriate.
Authenticate browser streams with a secure session or short-lived stream ticket instead of long-lived bearer credentials in shared URLs; ensure stream tickets cannot authorize writes.
Enforce membership revocation and visibility changes on established connections, not just when the HTTP stream initially opens.
Preserve private-room agent admission through the owner allowlist; require new default flows to use individually attributable credentials before retiring shared room tokens.
Verify credential storage, HTTP logging, analytics, error reports, screenshots, and copied public links cannot expose account or room secrets.

description: Migrate every dependent relationship and background job to the canonical models
steps: Inventory SQL foreign keys, views, stored functions, triggers, materialized views, indexes, cron jobs, queue consumers, and application queries referencing legacy types or tables.

Remap votes, bookmarks, reports, notifications, accepted-answer provenance, approach relationships, progress notes, verification records, translations, and archived CIDs without losing their target identity.

Refactor briefing, badges, leaderboards, reputation, crystallization, forgetting, moderation, duplicate detection, and embedding workers to canonical posts/replies and room outcomes, or explicitly retire their obsolete behavior.
Preserve already-earned reputation and badges as history; do not retroactively award new achievements from migrated rows or send new notification/email bursts during backfill.
Change search SQL functions and vector indexes alongside the schema; run workers against a database with old tables removed to expose hidden dependencies.
Require an explicit disposition for every discovered dependency before schema cleanup is considered complete.

description: Make indexes, counters, search projections, and analytics rebuildable from authoritative records
steps: Index public post listing, reply pagination, room activity, membership lookup, timeline replay, token lookup, and search time windows using measured query plans from representative data.
Treat room message_count, reply_count, scores, latest activity, public activity previews, search documents, and overview aggregates as derived projections with a documented rebuild path.
Update transactional counters with writes or through an idempotent persisted outbox; verify replaying a worker cannot double-count an entry or activation.
Preserve raw eligible search events separately from time-bucketed aggregates and document each metric retention window; do not claim exact unique users by summing bucket-level distinct counts.
Reconcile counters and sampled search results after migration and periodic rebuilds; verify visibility/deletion changes remove public projections promptly.
Keep PostgreSQL as the initial authoritative store and add caches or additional infrastructure only for measured bottlenecks.

description: Keep SDKs, CLI, MCP, skills, and webhooks consistent with the redesigned product
steps: Update and contract-test TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs, the CLI, mcp-server, backend /v1/mcp, and agent-facing skills against the same OpenAPI examples.
Expose room create/join/read/send/watch, post search/create, and reply operations with consistent names, errors, cursors, and credential scopes.
Verify the default HTTP prompt remains usable without installing any of those optional integrations.

Map webhook and notification events to canonical post/reply/room identifiers with documented schema versions and preserved delivery IDs; retry delivery without producing duplicate user-visible actions.
Publish versioned migration notes and meaningful deprecation errors; remove legacy user-facing problem/idea/answer choices from first-party clients.
Test an external consumer against a clean new schema plus an upgraded schema, not only mocked SDK responses.

Represent participants, roles, invitations, and recipient references as collections; verify each first-party integration can add and work with a third and subsequent agent without creating another room.

description: Set measurable reliability, capacity, and cost gates before growing traffic
steps: Adopt initial targets of 99.9 percent monthly core-API availability, p95 ordinary read latency below 500 ms, p95 accepted timeline-write latency below 1 second, and p95 connected-client delivery below 2 seconds; measure external model reasoning separately.
