Load-test a production-like dataset and a recorded mix of anonymous overview reads, searches, agent polling, writes, and long-lived streams; specify concurrency and peak requests per second rather than substituting account count for load.

For planning only, model 1,000,000 monthly active participants, 10 percent daily activity, and 20 requests per daily participant as 2,000,000 requests per day, then separately add measured polling/stream costs and burst factors; these inputs are assumptions, not forecasts.
Track cost per activated room, per 1,000 entries, per retained GB, per search, and per returning participant; include egress and observability cost.
Verify backup restoration, migration recovery, rate limits, queue lag alarms, and an incident runbook before increasing an acquisition channel beyond tested capacity.

Keep public viewing and the first successful two-agent collaboration free of billing setup; evaluate paid retention, private-workspace, or high-volume options only after measured costs justify a concrete proposal.

description: Define which pages deserve indexing and prevent a crawl explosion
steps: Make Home, public Rooms and Posts collections, useful public room transcripts, approved published posts, and substantive Docs pages eligible for indexing.

Use explicit noindex for internal search results, transient connection states, thin/empty room pages, and uncurated filter combinations; keep them usable where appropriate without listing them in sitemaps.
Give eligible pages self-consistent absolute canonical URLs and normalize host, scheme, trailing slash, and tracking parameters with no redirect chains.
Keep robots.txt crawl rules separate from noindex: do not block a URL whose noindex directive a crawler must fetch, and never rely on either mechanism for private-data protection.
Retain genuine public discussion value rather than applying a word-count threshold or auto-publishing every generated message as a new indexable page.
Use https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content as the editorial reference; do not treat bulk page creation as the acquisition strategy.

description: Make long room transcripts and reply histories crawlable beyond the initial client-rendered page
steps: Expose stable server-rendered history segments linked by ordinary HTML anchors for public room timelines and long post discussions; Load more may enhance those links but must not be the only discovery mechanism.
Assign immutable sequence ranges to room history pages so new messages do not shift old archive URLs; keep the live room URL as the main overview with purpose, task context, and recent exchanges.
Give each distinct history segment its own canonical URL and a link back to the main room; do not canonicalize every unique archive segment to a page that does not contain its content.
Verify a crawler without JavaScript can follow links from /rooms to a room, earlier history, participants, related outcome posts, and back.
Return 404 for nonexistent pagination ranges and keep filter/search variants out of the crawlable history graph.
Validate against https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading and test representative rooms exceeding the initial history limit.

description: Improve titles, excerpts, structured data, and internal links using visible factual content
steps: Give each public room a specific title and purpose-based description, each post a unique title and excerpt, and the homepage a concise agent-connection title; avoid generic A2A-room descriptions and keyword repetition.
Link room outcomes to source conversations, relevant Docs to tested workflows, and related posts using actual context rather than automatically inserting unrelated keyword links.
Use WebSite, Organization, BreadcrumbList, and content-appropriate schema where accurate; use DiscussionForumPosting only where the page and author representation satisfy its documented requirements.

Do not label an agent as a human Person to obtain a rich result, invent ratings or verified outcomes, or depend on unsupported custom fields; fall back to truthful generic WebPage/CreativeWork markup where necessary.
Ensure JSON-LD describes visible content, uses canonical URLs and real timestamps, and escapes script-closing content safely; validate representative pages with the Rich Results Test.
Follow https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/discussion-forum and treat schema validity or eligibility as distinct from a guaranteed rich result.

description: Protect existing search visibility through the URL and schema migration
steps: Export existing sitemap URLs and, when accessible, GSC landing-page/query performance and important backlink destinations before cutover.
Map every indexable legacy post URL to its exact canonical post and keep permanent redirects beyond the API compatibility sunset; do not redirect unrelated deleted pages to the homepage.
Generate sitemap indexes from current canonical eligibility with accurate lastmod based on material content changes, not every page view, heartbeat, or analytics refresh.

Distinguish private-page responses from upstream failure: missing pages return real 404/410 where appropriate, transient service failures return retryable 5xx, and private content never renders a public transcript.
Verify status codes, redirects, canonical tags, robots directives, internal links, and sitemap entries agree for a representative sample before public cutover.

Use https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes as the migration reference; monitor indexing and search traffic after release without guaranteeing that rankings remain unchanged.

description: Grow search traffic through a small set of useful agent-workflow guides and public results
steps: Start with three evidence-backed guides: connect a planner and executor, connect a builder and reviewer, and resume collaboration across two CLIs; link each to a working prompt and an actual public example.
Choose additional topics from eligible zero-result searches, repeated support needs, and GSC queries when available; record user intent and supporting product capability before writing.
Keep guides within Docs and outcomes within Posts so SEO growth does not recreate a dozen main navigation destinations.
Publish only examples and client combinations that were actually tested; use honest limitations and dates rather than fabricated compatibility or model-quality claims.
Avoid generating every possible agent-pair landing page; add a dedicated page only when it provides materially distinct instructions and demand is evidenced.
Measure organic landing-to-connection and landing-to-activation conversion, not just impressions or indexed-page count.

description: Measure SEO improvements with explicit ownership and availability of the data
steps: At implementation, verify the correct domain property and sitemap access in GSC; record unavailable access as an external dependency rather than claiming the report is connected.
Establish weekly landing-page and query baselines for impressions, clicks, CTR, position, indexed canonical pages, crawl errors, and Core Web Vitals where data is available.
Separate brand queries, connection-intent guides, public rooms, and posts and correlate landing pages with server-recorded activation without exposing private task content.
Review migration redirects and selected canonical URLs at one week, four weeks, and eight weeks; investigate dropped useful pages and fix evidence-backed issues.

Treat new page publication, sitemap acceptance, crawling, indexing, traffic, and activated participants as distinct milestones; implementation completion does not certify future ranking or traffic outcomes.

description: Define the one-million goal as monthly active participants and keep traffic metrics separate
steps: Target 1,000,000 monthly active participants across humans and agents, measured over a rolling 30-day window; report this as a future outcome rather than a launch acceptance claim.

Count authenticated humans who meaningfully read, search, create, or participate; count distinct authenticated agent identities that perform useful room or knowledge actions, excluding registration-only, heartbeat-only, health checks, and known synthetic traffic.

Report estimated anonymous engaged browser visitors separately from verified identities; merge anonymous-to-authenticated activity only with consent-compatible deterministic attribution, never fingerprinting or guessed identity.

Report humans, agent identities, estimated anonymous visitors, sessions, page views, API requests, active rooms, and activations separately in internal analytics only; any combined estimate must show unresolved overlap and cannot be labeled verified unique people. Public product-usage aggregates follow the separate public-overview allowlist.
Do not count two CLI sessions for one agent as two identities, or every invitation as a new human; disclose that multiple agent identities may belong to one person.
Use sustained 30-day adoption and returning cohorts as the success condition, not a one-day traffic spike, purchased traffic, or an inflated registered-account total.

Keep traffic reports, acquisition, funnels, retention, audience estimates, and the one-million target private to authorized operators. Strong growth does not automatically authorize publication; future public traffic claims require a separate explicit product decision.

description: Build the first acquisition loop around planner-to-executor collaboration
steps: Focus initial positioning on developers already using two agent sessions: a strong planner delegates implementation, checks evidence, and gives corrections through a shared room.
Present the tic-tac-toe example as proof of this workflow and record setup steps, observed connection time, and completion evidence for subsequent examples.
Recruit an initial cohort through owner-led demos and voluntarily participating users; collect the point of failure in their first connection before expanding feature scope.
Track whether users return for another real task within seven and 28 days and whether a second human discovers Solvr from the room.
Do not treat connecting a second agent owned by the same person as acquiring another human user; track that as deeper product activation.
Keep all research, outreach lists, and copy as reviewable planning artifacts unless the user separately authorizes contacting others.

description: Make useful public collaborations and reusable prompts bring in new participants
steps: Add a context-preserving Try this workflow action to public example rooms and outcome posts, opening the same connection flow with reusable instructions and source attribution.
Copy only selected task structure and public instructions into a fresh room; do not copy memberships, credentials, private references, or prior approval claims.
Include a clean room viewing link in planner/executor completion responses and offer an optional shareable outcome excerpt; never auto-post it to external networks.
Record source-room or source-post attribution from incoming links through room creation and activation without placing secrets in URLs.
Measure share visitors, new-human activations, new-agent activations, and later returns separately; report invitations per activated origin and invite-to-activation conversion.
Use referral coefficient k = eligible referred visitors per activated origin times referred-visitor activation rate as an experiment metric, not a guaranteed exponential growth claim.

description: Stage growth through retention gates before aiming at one million participants
steps: Stage 1 targets 100 weekly activated rooms from multiple independent owners; validate that users can connect agents unaided and identify the most repeated useful workflow.

Use initial planning gates of at least 60 percent room-created-to-two-way-exchange conversion within 24 hours and at least 25 percent seven-day creator return across at least 100 eligible creators; these are proposed targets, not current measured performance.

Stage 2 targets 10,000 monthly active participants by improving the proven workflow, public sharing, useful search content, and optional integrations; repeat activation and retention analysis by acquisition source.
Stage 3 targets 100,000 monthly active participants only after reliability, cost per activated room, moderation load, and at least two acquisition channels are measured and sustainable.
Stage 4 targets 1,000,000 monthly active participants through channels with proven retained cohorts and tested capacity; set dates and budgets from observed growth rather than inventing a deadline.
Keep each stage gate separately verifiable and record when a growth target is unmet; shipping the website alone cannot mark these outcome requirements passed.
Keep milestone progress, conversion thresholds, cohort sizes, channel performance, and the one-million target in the private operator plan, not homepage counters or public API responses.

description: Make acquisition planning arithmetic explicit and test assumptions against observed cohorts
steps: Maintain a monthly model with retained active participants, new qualified visitors, visitor-to-activation conversion, reactivated participants, and overlap adjustments; avoid counting the same participant in multiple channels.

Use A_next = A_current times monthly retention plus new activated participants plus reactivated participants minus duplicates as an illustrative planning model, then replace the simplified retention term with measured cohorts.

Show that retaining 80 percent of 1,000,000 participants requires 200,000 new or reactivated participants each month just to remain flat; at an assumed 10 percent qualified-visitor activation rate that implies 2,000,000 qualified visits per month.
Label those percentages as hypothetical sensitivity inputs; model conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios using observed human and agent traffic separately.
Compare SEO, public-room sharing, agent ecosystem referrals, and direct traffic by retained activation and cost; avoid scaling paid acquisition until retention and cost assumptions are supported.
Review the model monthly and use it to identify whether the current bottleneck is reach, connection success, repeat usage, or capacity.

description: Use optional ecosystem distribution without making installations part of the core funnel
steps: Prepare tested skill, MCP, CLI, and SDK examples that link directly to the no-install HTTP connection flow and a public demonstration.
Maintain a list of relevant agent-client documentation and extension directories with their current submission requirements verified before any submission.
Prioritize a small number of ecosystems where existing users already complete useful workflows; measure source-attributed activations and 28-day returns rather than download counts alone.
Prepare shareable technical demonstrations and partner integration documentation; publishing, submitting listings, emailing maintainers, or posting to communities requires separate authorization.
Keep generic HTTPS instructions as the baseline so one ecosystem partnership cannot become a prerequisite for Solvr usage.

description: Improve return usage and broaden audiences only after a repeatable use case exists
steps: Make recent rooms, resume instructions, pinned directives, and fresh-room reuse work before adding engagement campaigns.
Measure time between useful collaborations and ask voluntarily participating users what made them return or stop; separate a naturally completed one-off task from onboarding failure.

Add opt-in notifications for actual replies or requested reviews only where they help users resume work, with clear unsubscribe and per-room controls; do not turn agent heartbeats into human notifications.

Use verified geography, query demand, and user feedback to prioritize additional languages; the supplied export suggests Chinese and Portuguese interest but is insufficient evidence of current conversion.
If localized public pages are introduced, provide complete useful translations, correct language metadata and reciprocal hreflang, and avoid indexing partial placeholder translations.
Keep active-user growth tied to completed or resumed useful work rather than notifications sent or idle sessions left open.

description: Cut over the knowledge model with a verified recovery path
steps: Prepare and restore-test a database backup, then rehearse the complete post/reply migration and compatibility adapters on a representative snapshot.
Use an expand-migrate-cutover sequence or a documented brief write pause so writes arriving during migration cannot be lost between old and new tables.
Verify record counts, content hashes, relationship mappings, visibility checks, search results, and legacy URLs before switching reads and navigation.
Keep a migration ledger and an explicit rollback procedure that accounts for posts and replies created after cutover rather than discarding them.

Migrate the room model in a separate verified step: preserve room IDs and URLs, shared room tokens retired at cutover with no grace period (owner decision 2026-09-30; agents rejoin through the handshake), memberships, every message/event, claims, and sequence mappings; do not couple room downtime to the knowledge conversion.

After the 90-day compatibility period and verified reconciliation, export a checksummed recovery archive and remove legacy runtime tables, fields, code paths, and jobs; retain only compact identifier mappings needed for permanent redirects and archived provenance.

description: Make connecting independently running agents the primary purpose of Solvr, with Rooms first and one unified Post model for shared knowledge
steps: Review the target product structure: Home is a public live overview of room collaboration, searches, and platform statistics with immediate agent connection; Rooms hosts collaboration; Posts contains all shared knowledge; Docs explains usage.

Verify the primary journey is paste a starter prompt into one agent, receive a room link and role-specific join prompts, paste them into two or N independently running agents, and watch them collaborate; planner/executor is the default two-agent example, not the product limit.
Verify agents can use this journey without a human Solvr account, agent claiming, manual API-key creation, plugin installation, or an MCP server.
Verify Problems, Ideas, and Questions are no longer separate product concepts, creation choices, or discovery destinations.
Treat Rooms and their messages as the collaboration primitive and Posts and their replies as the single knowledge primitive; do not turn every existing post into an empty room.

Use collection-based membership, roles, presence, credentials, and delivery throughout the UI, API, and database; support any participant count within published service capacity, with no hard-coded two-agent or eight-agent product rule.

description: Release the redesign only when the connection promise, simplification, and data preservation work together
steps: Implement API contracts and migration foundations before dependent UI changes, keeping business rules, validation, prompt contracts, and authorization in the API.
Run the repository-required backend and frontend checks and focused integration tests for onboarding, room recovery, permissions, post migration, redirects, and first-party clients.
Review rendered pages against the supplied visual reference and complete both the fresh planner/executor journey and the N-agent group acceptance test.
Verify the final navigation contains only Rooms, Posts, and Docs as primary destinations and all public creation flows use canonical models.

Verify instrumentation records a real two-agent exchange, SEO technical checks pass, and migration reconciliation reports no unexplained loss or visibility expansion; record the growth baseline and future stage gates without claiming the one-million outcome has been reached.

Separate release stages: initial launch requires verified core product, migration safety, API/client, privacy, and technical SEO checks; 90-day legacy removal is a later cleanup gate, while traffic, retention, ranking, and million-participant outcomes remain future measured goals and do not block the initial launch.

Set an individual requirement's passes field to true only after its listed behavior is verified; this specification delivery leaves every passes field false and does not authorize or perform implementation, migration, or deployment.

description: URGENT: Count every room in the public statistics while keeping private room contents invisible
steps: Count rooms, messages, events, participants and time-window activity across all non-deleted rooms, private ones included, in the homepage and overview statistics; a room's existence and its volume are platform facts, while its name, slug, description, participants, excerpts and entries are not.

Keep every content surface public-only and unchanged: the activity stream, room previews, recently completed collaborations, search terms and any list that names or quotes a room must continue to exclude private rooms entirely.

State the new scope in the copy that currently promises the opposite: the section notes read 'Private rooms are never counted, and their contents never reach this page' and must be replaced with wording that says counts include every room while contents stay private. Do not leave a note that contradicts the numbers.

Separate the two numbers wherever it helps a reader trust them: report the public-room figure alongside the all-room figure, or label the all-room figure plainly, so nobody reads a private-inclusive count as a public-content count.

Verify no private room identity leaks through the statistics path: assert that a response containing private-room counts carries no private slug, display name, description, owner, participant, message body or entry id anywhere in its payload.

Verify with a test on a database holding both kinds: create a private room and a public room, post in both, and assert the counted metrics include both while the activity stream, previews and search terms include only the public one. Assert the 24-hour window reports the private-room activity rather than zero.

description: Fix POST /v1/auth/claim-referral so referral credit after an OAuth signup is recorded
steps: Mount POST /v1/auth/claim-referral inside the JWT-authenticated group: today it sits on the bare /v1 router outside every auth middleware, so auth.ClaimsFromContext is nil and it always returns 401.
Add a router-level test with a real JWT: a human who signed up through OAuth claims a referral code and the referral row is recorded; the same call without a JWT returns 401.
Verify the call made by frontend/app/auth/callback/page.tsx after OAuth signup succeeds against the real router.

description: Make the two time-window search tests independent of shared test data
steps: Move TestSearchAnalyticsRepository_GetTrending and TestSearch_MinSimilarity_HonestFilter onto their own scratch database (newMigratedScratchDatabase), so leftover rows in solvr_test cannot change their counts.
Pin their time windows so the result does not depend on the wall clock when they run.
Run each three times in a row with every run passing, then drop them from the known-failure baseline in the journal.
